newsitem.title: UK: Caribs crude tankers continue to rise, others flat.
newsitem.headline: Caribs crude tankers continue to rise, others flat.

text.p: Caribs/upcoast dirty tanker rates continued to firm on Thursday, with charterers apparently convinced that last week's decline was well and truly over, brokers said.
Upcoast 70,000 tonne rates rose towards the W180 mark after gaining some 10 points on Wednesday.
"Charterers are hot and heavy to buy. They saw the price falling last week and they seem to think it isn't going to fall any further," one broker said.
Upcoast 70,000 tonners have been on a sharp upward trend recently despite last week's fall.
According to New York-based Rigos Chartering Inc, they averaged just W131.6 in February and W148.08 in 1996.
But 50,000 tonne fuel oil vessels dipped to W190/195 despite the rise in crude rates in this sector.
Middle East very large crude carriers (VLCCs) were steady but with a slightly softer tone.
"There is a bit of nervousness around. Owners are feeling that March is finished. But there are still come cargoes to come out and there are three weeks to go," one broker said.
Mideast/west VLCCs remained at W52.5/W55, with vessels to Japan at about W60 and to Singapore at W57.5.
An ultra-large crude carrier, the Hellespont Capitol, was fixed with 380,000 tonnes to the U.S. Gulf at W47.5 for Vela, loading March 15.
West Africa was quiet but stable with VLCCs at W72.5 to the U.S. Gulf and 130,000 tonne vessels at about W102.5.
The Mediterranean and inter-U.K./Cont were also quiet, with 80,000 tonnes in both sectors at W115 and million barrel (130,000 tonnes) ships at about W100.
Fuel oil edged down to W200 from W215 for 25,000 tonnes inter-U.K./Cont on low enquiry, with Med rates stable at W200.
